paper.title: Dynamic Assortment Optimization with Changing Contextual Information

settings.name_in_paper: Dynamic assortment optimization under changing contextual MNL model
unmapped: Actions are assortments S of at most m (paper's K) items out of K (paper's N) items; customer choice follows a multinomial logit model with utilities v_tj^T theta_0; learner observes the purchased item (or no purchase) and earns its revenue r_tj in [0,1]
Revenues r_tj and features v_tj change over time; features i.i.d. from a distribution with lambda_min(E vv^T) >= lambda_0 during the first T0 exploration rounds (A1), adversarial afterwards
Assumption (A2): ratio of choice probabilities of any two options in any assortment bounded by rho
Algorithm tuning uses lambda_0, rho, nu (feature norm bound) and cardinality K
settings.definition_quote: p_{\theta_0,t}(j|S) = \frac{\exp\{v_{tj}^\top\theta_0\}}{1+\sum_{k\in S} \exp\{v_{tk}^\top\theta_0\}} ... \mathrm{Regret}(\{S_t\}_{t=1}^T) =\mathbb E^\pi\sum_{t=1}^T R_t(S_t^*) - R_t(S_t) where S_t^*=\arg\max_{S\subseteq[N], |S|\leq K} R_t(S)

settings.name_in_paper: Dynamic assortment optimization under contextual MNL model (lower bound)
unmapped: Assortments of at most m (paper's K) items with MNL choice feedback; hard instance uses time-invariant features and revenues r_ti = 1
settings.definition_quote: there is a worst-case problem instance with $N\asymp K\cdot 2^d$ items and uniformly bounded feature and coefficient vector (i.e., $\|v_{ti}\|_2\leq 1$ and $\|\theta_0\|_2\leq 1$ for all $i\in[N]$, $t\in[T]$)

algorithms.name: MLE-UCB with an (alpha, eps, delta)-approximation oracle for the assortment step

bound.expression_latex: C_1\left[ d\sqrt{T}\cdot \log(\lambda_0^{-1}\rho\nu TK)+ {d^2\lambda_0^{-2}\rho^4\nu^2 K^2\log T}\right] + C_2

symbols.rho: bound on ratio of choice probabilities (Assumption A2)
symbols.lambda_0: lower bound on min eigenvalue of feature covariance during exploration (A1)

conditions: (A1) ||v_tj||_2 <= nu; for t <= T0 features i.i.d. with lambda_min(E vv^T) >= lambda_0
(A2) p(j|S)/p(j'|S) <= rho for all assortments |S| <= K
tuning: T0 ≍ max{nu^2 d log T/lambda_0^2, rho^2 (d+log T)/(tau^2 lambda_0)}
omega ≍ sqrt(d log(rho nu T K))

results.notes: Universal constants C1, C2 unspecified, recorded as O. Bound independent of the number of items N. Exact combinatorial step requires enumerating all subsets (exponential); polynomial approximations given separately. Regret defined via expected revenues, so pseudo-regret.

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: Suppose $d$ is divisible by 4. There exists a universal constant $C_0>0$ such that for any sufficiently large $T$ and policy $\pi$, there is a worst-case problem instance with $N\asymp K\cdot 2^d$ items and uniformly bounded feature and coefficient vector (i.e., $\|v_{ti}\|_2\leq 1$ and $\|\theta_0\|_2\leq 1$ for all $i\in[N]$, $t\in[T]$) such that the regret of $\pi$ is lower bounded by $C_2\cdot d\sqrt{T}/K$.

results.notes: Minimax construction via subsets W of size d/4 with Pinsker inequality.

symbols.alpha_apx: multiplicative approximation factor of the oracle
symbols.eps_apx: additive approximation error of the oracle
symbols.delta_apx: failure probability of the oracle per round

tuning: (alpha, eps, delta)-approximation algorithm used for the combinatorial step

source.label: lem:approx
source.quote: Suppose an $(\alpha,\varepsilon,\delta)$-approximation algorithm is used instead of exact optimization in the MLE-UCB policy at each time period $t$. Then its regret can be upper bounded by \alpha\cdot \mathrm{Regret}^* + \varepsilon T + \delta T^2 + O(1)

results.notes: Reduction lemma expressed relative to Theorem 1's bound; compute polynomial for the DP-based oracles (d=1 exact DP; multivariate randomized).
